review_notes: The file has only two plain, non-recursive `def`s: `angularSourceFunction` and `angularCorrectionFunction`. It has no simp lemmas, no attributes and no rewrite rules, so there is nothing to check for orientation, competing rules or cycles. I read the downstream uses in `LocalPeriodicCorrector.lean` (around lines 191–219) and `ExplicitPeriodicFormula.lean` (lines 45–82). Those uses unfold the definitions explicitly with `simp only [angularSourceFunction, ...]`, `unfold angularCorrectionFunction` or `simp only [angularCorrectionFunction, map_add]`. The surrounding proofs mostly use `change`, `rw` and `congr`, so I found no repeated rewriting that a canonical simp lemma would clearly shorten. The definitions are not reducible and are not simp-tagged, so they are not expanded unwantedly. Adding simp attributes to them would be speculative. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out a minor ergonomic gain from a named equation lemma, but the sources do not support a concrete finding under this rubric.
